method: One row per item of docs/parity/inventory-ui.json, same order and ids. Each item's details (message, property, timing, UI rule) were mapped to the Home Assistant surface that plays the same role: entity platforms (light.py, switch.py, cover.py, climate.py, sensor.py, binary_sensor.py, event.py, scene.py, button.py, select.py, number.py), the central entities on the mesh device (JungHomeCentralEntity subclasses: JungHomeAllLights / AllSockets / AllBlinds / AllThermostats), config entities (config_entities.py PropertyReader / LockFunctionEntity / EdgeDetectionEntity, keep_awake.py), coordinator.py connect-time sequence (_chunked refresh, _send_time, async_follow_gateway, _missed_answer/_heard_from reachability, energy poll), energy_history.py, and the actions in services.py / mesh_config.py / onboard.py / schedules.py. Lookups: grep -n in custom_components/junghome_ble and tools/ for the opcode / property id (PropertySpec(0x....) in jhmesh/properties.py, const.py constants), for the class or function named in the row, and for the attribute/translation key the item's text maps to (strings.json). Code refs are resolved mechanically: each is a (file, regex) pair, the first matching line is cited (generator: tools-less script kept outside the repo; rerun = same pairs). Tests: an AST index of every tests/**/test_*.py function (name + body text); a test is cited when it drives the cited code path and asserts the behaviour (checked by name/body), and every cited name was verified to exist in the index. Status rules: implemented = the item's behaviour (encoding, range, sequence, timing, or its HA-native equivalent where the item is a pure UI affordance HA core provides - brightness/colour-temperature step, climate slider, entity availability) is reproduced by cited code that a cited test exercises; deliberate improvements that keep the effect (CTL Temperature Set instead of CTL Set with a stale lightness, lock read-back after a timed lock, reference-run read-back, reading every load's state at connect instead of favourites only) count as implemented. partial = code exists but a behaviour of the item differs or is missing (text in `missing`). gap = nothing implements it. na = only with a concrete design reason: cloud project sync, Android permissions, app-role banners, analytics, phone-local display preferences (DeviceInfoEntity L7/c: card flags, price, notes), pure navigation state, dead strings. Shared shortfalls reuse one fixed sentence so a rerun groups them identically: favourites (isFavorite in the export meta), room-level central control, thermostat binding (RtrConnectionMode), firmware update availability, PIR sensitivity steps/scoping, button layout 0x5001, key-mode-3 property targets 0x5006-0x5008, sleep state, lock-state visibility on loads, detector forced mode on the load, lock time-limit seconds, chunk pause, room/scene icons, multi-room membership, 5 s on-page refresh, Move vs Delta Set for blinds. Each partial/gap row carries `feasibility`: whether it can be implemented and verified without the physical installation. Facts re-checked in jadx for this ledger: ConfigurationConsumptionViewModel$resetTotalConsumption$1 resets u8.a (0x006D) before u8.b (0x006A); PowerConsumptionViewModel$requestData$1 gates each read on the device's capability interfaces; assets/updates/*.gbl bundle the firmware images with versions in their names. Verification pass (adversarial): every gap/na/partial row re-checked by grepping custom_components, tools and tests for the opcode/property/feature under other names; 20+ implemented rows re-derived from jadx (reachability: MeshMessengerImpl$handleError$1 + FlowOperatorsKt.sendWithTimeoutRetry; boost poll: RoomTemperatureViewModel$observeCompatible$1 FlowOperatorsKt.h; detector brightness: const.DETECTOR_BRIGHTNESS_POLL) and demoted where timing or threshold differs: ui:state:devicereachability, ui:state:presencebrightnesscapability, ui:vm:roomtemperatureviewmodel.observecompatible, ui:vm:roomtemperatureviewmodel.requestboostfunction. Rows for the items appended by the inventory's STEP 6 reuse the shared sentences above (icons, firmware update, cloud, key-mode-3, device rename) and mirror the net ledger where the same use case is judged there (net:uc:checknameinput, net:uc:resetdevice, net:uc:removeinvaliddevices, net:uc:observeprojectbubbleindicators). Citations: every `code` entry is now `path::symbol` (docs/parity/README.md, Row schema), converted from `path:line` by reading each line in the tree its ledger line was written against (git blame), following it through every later re-pointing that kept the cited text and past the merges that re-pointed lines to other code, and naming the innermost symbol holding it; `tools/parity.py check` verifies each symbol is defined.

the app's rule: one request asked with the full budget (3 x 3 s) left unanswered marks the node unreachable at once (MeshMessengerImpl$handleError$1 sets failedMessagesCounter to 3), for the connect-time state Gets and every load command; any message from the node revives it. Deliberate differences: a command's miss counts only once the link watchdog's probe got an answer through the proxy (a proxy that stopped forwarding leaves every command unanswered: the link is dropped and no node is charged; the app has no such probe and would show each commanded device as No connection); a node heard from while it was asked stays reachable (the app would have completed the request on its D1 27 05 and reset the counter on any status); the one-attempt link keep-alive is no verdict (re-asked with the full budget after 60 s); vendor property reads do not count (a property a firmware lacks would make a working load unavailable; they leave their entity unknown); battery nodes are never marked (N1(): the app shows no 'No connection' for them either, and their keys work while asleep); an unreachable node is re-probed every 300 s (review-3 C3)

the three errors map to service errors (service_name_blank / service_invalid_room_name, service_name_not_allowed, service_room_exists / service_scene_exists); a device name that is taken is numbered, as the app does, and a device name the app refuses raises the device_name_rejected repair issue (the rename comes from the device registry, not from a service call). A rename (device, room, scene: the app's NameConfig sheet, fragment_name_config.xml app:maxLength="30", an InputFilter.LengthFilter) takes at most 30 Java chars (UTF-16 code units, name_length); a longer new name is refused as service_name_too_long (device rename: the device_name_rejected repair issue) instead of truncated as the LengthFilter does while typing - HA gets the name whole, and cutting it silently would write a name nobody typed. Creating a room or scene has no limit (the app's create screens set none), a name kept as it is is not checked again, and the limit is on the name typed: the app's number suffix may take the result past it, as in the app.

rows.note: REQUEST (state / property Get) and UPDATE (a load's OnOff / Lightness / CTL / CTL Temperature / Level Set) wait for the status the app's way: REQUEST_ATTEMPTS = 3 attempts of 3 s, the same PDU (same TID), matched on source element + status opcode; an unanswered command fails the action (device_not_reachable, worded for a node that may still turn out reachable) and marks the node unreachable once the link probe shows the proxy forwards. Deliberate differences: the movements are sent without waiting (the cover's Move Set, which the app never sends, and hold-to-dim's Move / Delta Set, unverified on air): whether a blind publishes its level at the start of a run or only at its end is unknown (control-and-state.md §5 Q2), so a waited-for movement could fail a working blind after 9 s and mark it unreachable; they keep the echo watch of group commands (a silent mesh makes the watchdog probe the proxy); without a link a command waits out the link-loss grace (review-3) instead of failing at once; group commands stay unacknowledged (as the app's central functions); the D1 27 05 substitute answer is not taken (msg:mech:waitforstatusmessage)

rows.note: The app reads power 0x0081 and the counters every 5 s while its consumption page is open. HA has no open page: power comes from the meter's publications, the counters are read every ENERGY_POLL_INTERVAL = 300 s, and homeassistant.update_entity on any meter sensor reads the load's Sensor Gets and counters at once (coordinator.async_refresh_meter; concurrent updates of one load share one read, and entity.JungHomeEntity.async_update asks a load's meter at most once per UPDATE_READ_INTERVAL = 2 s). A 5 s poll with nobody looking would only load the mesh (docs/ha-integration.md '## Data updates').

Deliberate difference, documented in docs/ha-integration.md ('### Climate', Presets row): the preset temperature is sent as the target first on every firmware (it works whether the firmware version is known or not), then 0x120B on 2.2.0.0 or newer as the app sends it; the app writes only 0x120B there.
